root_cause.text: The f81604 CAN USB interrupt URB callback in `f81604_read_int_callback()` failed to validate that `urb->actual_length` was at least the size of the expected interrupt data structure before accessing it, causing short URB payloads to be treated as valid data.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a new guard `if (urb->actual_length < sizeof(*data)) { ... goto resubmit_urb; }` and the CVE/commit message explicitly states that previously, when an interrupt URB was “not the correct length,” the driver would “attempt to treat the data as valid.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a short-packet check in the interrupt URB callback to warn and resubmit instead of processing undersized data.
intent_record.what: A new length check was added in f81604_read_int_callback() before processing the interrupt URB data: if urb->actual_length is smaller than sizeof(*data), the code logs a warning with netdev_warn() and jumps to resubmit_urb.
intent_record.how: This prevents the callback from using an interrupt buffer that is shorter than the expected data structure size, avoiding invalid or out-of-bounds access on short URBs and safely resubmitting the URB instead.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable logic is clearly present in `f81604_read_int_callback()`, so the snippet is sufficient. The function obtains `struct f81604_int_data *data = urb->transfer_buffer;` and, after checking only `urb->status`, it immediately dereferences fields from `data` in `if (data->isrc & (F81604_SJA1000_IRQ_DOI | F81604_SJA1000_IRQ_EI | F81604_SJA1000_IRQ_BEI | F81604_SJA1000_IRQ_EPI | F81604_SJA1000_IRQ_ALI))` and `if (priv->can.state != CAN_STATE_BUS_OFF && (data->isrc & F81604_SJA1000_IRQ_TI))`. There is no validation anywhere in this callback that `urb->actual_length` is at least `sizeof(*data)` before those accesses. This matches the root cause: short interrupt URB payloads would be treated as valid `struct f81604_int_data`. The fix is not present because, unlike `f81604_read_bulk_callback()` which explicitly checks `if (urb->actual_length != sizeof(*frame))`, `f81604_read_int_callback()` has no corresponding length check at all.
